manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses user next-item behavior and generative semantic IDs: it assigns each item a semantically meaningful tuple of codewords (Semantic ID), then trains a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model to predict the next interacted item's Semantic ID from IDs in the user session. The abstract does not establish use of hyperbolic geometry.
sources.evidence_note: arXiv metadata/abstract independently verifies title, identifier, and stated method. A linked author manuscript/full-text PDF is available, but its contents were not inspected for this report; therefore the evidence label is ABSTRACT, not FULL_TEXT.

sources.title: HMamba: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses sequential/next-item recommendation and hyperbolic geometry, proposing a curvature-aware hyperbolic selective state-space model. The abstract does not mention generative semantic IDs or autoregressive item-identifier decoding.
sources.evidence_note: arXiv metadata/abstract independently verifies the bibliographic record and abstract-level claims. PDF available but not inspected; not labeled FULL_TEXT.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses sequential recommendation and hyperbolic geometry, using a hyperbolic hypergraph convolutional network and multi-scale temporal item representations. It does not state use of generative semantic IDs.
sources.evidence_note: arXiv metadata/abstract independently verifies the bibliographic record and stated approach. PDF available but not inspected; not labeled FULL_TEXT.

sources.title: Time-aware Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network for Session-based Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Explicitly frames session-based recommendation as predicting users' next interested items and proposes a time-aware hyperbolic graph attention model over sessions. It does not state use of generative semantic IDs.
sources.evidence_note: arXiv metadata/abstract independently verifies title, identifier, and abstract-level claims. PDF available but not inspected; not labeled FULL_TEXT.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Autoregressively generate the next item's semantic identifier from the user's observed interaction sequence, while placing or regularizing the item-code representation in a hyperbolic space.
behavior_problem_candidates.why_behavior_first: The target is the next user-interacted item; semantic IDs are the generated target representation, and hyperbolic geometry is a candidate inductive bias for hierarchical preference/item structure.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Generate a next-item semantic ID conditioned on recent session behavior and temporal transitions, with hyperbolic geometry modeling hierarchical session/item relationships.
behavior_problem_candidates.why_behavior_first: Session-based next-item prediction is explicit in the hyperbolic sequential/session literature; TIGER-style semantic-ID generation supplies a distinct output mechanism, but no verified source here combines them.

limitations: No independently verified paper was found in the checked records that combines all three elements—user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs—in one method. The sources are adjacent strands, not proof of a published integrated approach.
Evidence labels are conservative: only arXiv API metadata and abstracts were inspected. Full-text PDFs are linked but were not read, so none of the entries is labeled FULL_TEXT.
No DOI was verified for these records; arXiv identifiers and stable abstract/PDF URLs are provided instead.
The bibliography is a focused candidate set, not an exhaustive systematic review. Absence from this set should not be interpreted as proof that no related work exists.
Do not interpret generative retrieval as automatically implying hyperbolic geometry, or hyperbolic sequential recommendation as automatically implying semantic-ID generation.
